football_evidence.question: Can Sam Houston’s pass rush get to Caden Creel?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Jacksonville State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.8 of the 8.0 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.

When Sam Houston has the ball (the red zone): Sam Houston’s offense succeeds on 24.5% of its red-zone plays, and Jacksonville State’s defense allows success on 39.7% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.5%).

When Sam Houston has the ball (big plays through the air): Sam Houston’s offense turns 6.4% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Jacksonville State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.3% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).
contradicting: When Jacksonville State has the ball (third down): Jacksonville State’s offense converts 40.1% of its third downs, and Sam Houston’s defense allows opponents to convert 30.0% of their third downs (FBS average 39.6%).
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Sam Houston’s secondary No. 22 nationally and Jacksonville State’s No. 59.
EdgeDesk’s position-group ratings put Sam Houston’s pass defense No. 37 nationally and Jacksonville State’s No. 73.

quarterbacks: Caden Creel has completed 140 of 209 passes (67.0%) for 1,746 yards, 8.4 yards per attempt, 13 touchdowns and 8 interceptions in eight games for Jacksonville State, and has been sacked on 8 of 217 dropbacks.

Landyn Locke has completed 146 of 238 passes (61.3%) for 1,650 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 12 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in seven games for Sam Houston, and has been sacked on 16 of 254 dropbacks.
DJ Bailey has completed 20 of 38 passes (52.6%) for 258 yards, 6.8 yards per attempt, no touchdowns and no interceptions in two games for Sam Houston, and has been sacked on 5 of 43 dropbacks.
